title: How we measure star distances
info: Nearby stars seem to shift a tiny bit when Earth moves from one side of its orbit to the other. That shift is called parallax.
A bigger shift means a closer star. A tiny shift means a farther star.
Parallax works well only for nearby stars. Farther stars need other clues, such as how bright they truly are.
